questions.q: According to the octet rule, atoms tend to…
options: lose, gain or share electrons to get eight electrons in the outer shell
take up eight protons in the nucleus
questions.explain: To reach a stable noble-gas-like octet, atoms transfer or share electrons (two for H).

questions.q: How many valence electrons are there in the CO₃²⁻ ion?
questions.explain: 4 (C) + 3×6 (O) + 2 (for the charge) = 24.

questions.q: What is the formal charge on the central oxygen of O₃ (as in O=O⁺–O⁻)?
questions.explain: F.C. = 6 − 2 − ½×6 = +1 (one lone pair and three bonding pairs).

questions.q: In which molecule does the central atom have an incomplete octet?
questions.explain: In BF₃ boron has only 6 electrons around it. PCl₅ has 10 (an expanded octet).

questions.q: The lattice enthalpy of NaCl is 788 kJ mol⁻¹. What does this mean?
options: 788 kJ is needed to separate 1 mol of solid NaCl into gaseous Na⁺ and Cl⁻
The ionisation enthalpy of Na is 788 kJ mol⁻¹
The melting point of NaCl is 788 K
The electron gain enthalpy of Cl is −788 kJ mol⁻¹
questions.explain: Lattice enthalpy is the energy needed to break the crystal into gaseous ions.

questions.q: Forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ costs +147.1 kJ mol⁻¹. Why is NaCl still stable?
options: Forming the crystal lattice releases −788 kJ mol⁻¹
questions.explain: −788 + 147.1 is negative — the overall process releases energy.

questions.q: What is the order of bond lengths of C–C, C=C and C≡C?
questions.explain: Higher bond order, shorter bond: 154 > 133 > 120 pm.

questions.q: Which has the highest bond enthalpy?
questions.explain: N≡N is a triple bond (order 3) — 946.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.q: What is the length of each O–O bond in O₃, and why?
options: 148 and 121 pm — one single, one double bond
questions.explain: Experimentally both are 128 pm — the hybrid of I and II.

questions.q: Which molecule has zero dipole moment?
questions.explain: BF₃ is trigonal planar — three equal B–F moments cancel.

questions.q: In H₂O the H–O–H angle is 104.5° and μ = 1.85 D. What would μ be if the angle were 180°?
questions.explain: The two O–H moments would point in opposite directions and cancel (like CO₂): μ = 2 × 1.51 × cos 90° = 0.

questions.q: What are the shape and bond angle of NH₃?
questions.explain: The lp–bp repulsion of one lone pair closes the angle from 109.5° to 107°.

questions.q: What is the shape of XeF₄?
questions.explain: AB₄E₂: six pairs arranged octahedrally with the two lone pairs opposite each other — square planar.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of repulsion in VSEPR?
questions.explain: A lone pair is held by one nucleus only and spreads out, so lp–lp repulsion is the largest.

questions.q: What are the hybridisation of carbon in C₂H₄ and the number of σ and π bonds in the C=C bond?
options: sp²; one σ and one π
sp; one σ and two π
questions.explain: The sp² orbitals form the σ bond; sideways overlap of the unhybridised 2p orbitals forms the π bond.

questions.q: How many σ and π bonds are there in C₂H₂?
questions.explain: Two C–H plus the C–C = 3 σ bonds; the C≡C adds two π bonds.

questions.q: What are the hybridisations of the central atoms in PCl₅ and SF₆?
questions.explain: PCl₅: 5 σ bonds — sp³d (bipyramid); SF₆: 6 σ bonds — sp³d² (octahedron).

questions.q: What are the bond order and magnetic behaviour of O₂⁻?
questions.explain: 17 electrons: N_b = 10, N_a = 7 → ½(10 − 7) = 1.5, with one unpaired electron in π*.

questions.q: According to MO theory, which molecule does not exist?
questions.explain: Be₂: (σ2s)²(σ*2s)² — bond order ½(4 − 4) = 0.

questions.q: Among the group 16 hydrides, which has the highest boiling point, and why?
options: H₂O — because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding
H₂Te — because of its larger molar mass
questions.explain: H₂O boils at 373 K; H₂S, H₂Se, H₂Te at 213, 232 and 271 K.
